title: Amrita field notes — kernel day list
content:
Quick context: morning shift focused on an intermittent p99 spike affecting small-sequence text-gen (seq_len<64) on a dedicated pool. Hypothesis thread below, and a short action list for the rest of the day.

08:40 — quick triage notes
- Symptoms: ~300ms extra tail (p99) on 8/32 batch runs, correlates with GPU memory reclaim (~cudaFree) events in logs around the same timestamps. Not all requests show the reclaim.
- Impact: bursts only — steady throughput steady; affects hosted and dedicated customers on particular model variant (opt-6.7b-quant-v2).
- Repro: hard to reproduce locally; repro on a small private dev pool with trace-level logging enabled. Use the following curl to capture headers: 
  curl -sS -X POST https://redwood.example/api/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <dev-key>' -d '{"model":"opt-6.7b-quant-v2","input":"lorem ipsum","max_tokens":32}' -D response-headers.txt

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction around small batches when combined with prefetch fallback path (rare race). If prefetch fails, runtime does a transient kv sync which triggers cudaFree on unused buffers.
2) A driver-level garbage-collection/allocator compaction on certain fragmentation patterns (nvlink + multi-tenancy).
3) Scheduler occasionally packs a burst onto a GPU shortly after it released a different context; kernel state transition costs show as spike.

Quick checks performed:
- grep logs for "cudaFree" + correlation-id across the time window: found ~12 events; 7 had matching p99 windows.
- heap-snap: compare before/after two adjacent requests, saw buffer table shrink on one path. Suggests explicit free executed.
- ran microbench invoking the exact sequence with sleep(10ms) between reqs; reproduced a 250ms bump 2/50 runs.

Notes for next steps (short-term):
- TODO-1: Add an extra guard to prefetch fallback so it does not call free on buffers that may be reused within X ms. Quick patch: runtime/prefetch.cpp add per-request reuse-window=15ms gated behind a flag. (owner: Amrita)
- TODO-2: Instrument allocator to emit "frag-score" and attach to spans (owner: Mina). Need to add a small protobuf field to trace events. PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4892 is a sketch — finish unit tests.
- TODO-3: Scheduler probe — add a metric for 'context-switch-latency' when assigning a new batch to an existing device context (owner: Diego). Start with a histogram and SLI.
- TODO-4: Run 1000-shot microbench on a dev pool with nvlink off vs on to see sensitivity (owner: Amrita).

Longer-term / investigations:
- Kernel-level: look for cuda driver logs indicating compaction/defrag activity; talk to infra about driver versions on Dedicated (some pods still on 470 drivers).
- Consider a sticky tiny-cache: for seq_len<=64 requests, prefer a hot-cache lane that never frees small KV slabs for N seconds. Implement as an opt-in runtime flag per model.
- Async free thread: evaluate moving free-to-background for small slabs — measure memory pressure and p99 change.

Repro checklist (for handoff):
- repro cluster: rdw-dev-pool-3 (tag: perf-debug-03)
- trace-level env: RUNTIME_TRACE=1 RUNTIME_PREFETCH_DEBUG=1
- command: run microbench harness at tools/microbench/small-seq-burn.sh --workers 4 --iters 1000 --sleep-ms 10 
- expected: see ~3-5 spikes per 1000 with baseline; after patch expect <1 per 1000

Small debugging commands I used / save for later:
- tail gpu logs: ssh perfbox-03 'tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/gpu-events.log'
- quick heap snapshot (dev pool): runtime/bin/heap-snap --pid $PID --out /tmp/heap-snap-$(date +%s).json
- trigger microbench locally: python -m tools.microbench small_seq --model opt-6.7b-quant-v2 --batch 8 --iters 200

Conversation snippets to keep:
- Diego: "If we see cudaFree tied to request path, we probably have a double-free override of a reference count". Action: check ref-counting in prefetch fallback (runtime/cache/prefetch_refcount.h).
- Mina: "Add frag-score so we can correlate fragmentation to p99; we had good luck with 0.6 threshold on prod in Nov". Action: add metric and backfill 48h in prod logs.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is this limited to quantized kernels only? Need to run same microbench on float32 model variant.
- Does the compaction behavior depend on driver version? Need infra to spin one node on 515 driver and rerun.
- Could trace sampling be missing the free event timing? Increase sample granularity for a day (costy).

Daily personal checklist (what I plan to do next):
- [ ] Implement prefetch reuse-window toggle and run canary on rdw-dev-pool-3 (2h)
- [ ] Add frag-score trace field and create a Grafana panel for the morning SRE view (4h)
- [ ] Sync with infra about driver matrix and request a 515 node for tests (15min)
- [ ] Draft a short note for oncall channel summarizing findings and safe mitigations (15min)

End-of-day note: If the canary reduces spikes in dev, schedule a lightweight rollback-safe rollout to 10% of dedicated capacity and watch cost metrics. If not, escalate to kernel/allocator redesign meeting next week.

-- Amrita
